blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: tentative distance — Current best-known route cost.
predecessor — Previous vertex on best path.

blocks.title: Observe
blocks.text: Dijkstra maintains tentative shortest distances from a start vertex. All edge weights must be non-negative.

blocks.title: Apply
blocks.text: Repeatedly finalise the unsettled node with smallest tentative distance, then relax outgoing edges to improve neighbour estimates.

blocks.title: Evaluate
blocks.text: Track predecessor nodes alongside distances to reconstruct the shortest route, not just its total cost.

blocks.title: Worked example · Update neighbours
blocks.text: Start with dist(P)=0 . Settle P (smallest unsettled value). Relax P→Q: Q=3 , predecessor Q←P. Relax P→R: R=8 , predecessor R←P. Remaining unsettled distances: Q=3, R=8.

blocks.title: Worked example · Improve the tentative route
blocks.text: Q=3 is the smallest unsettled distance. Via Q→R, the candidate is 3+2=5 . This beats R=8, so update R=5 and predecessor R←Q. Settled now: P,Q.

questions.feedback: tentative distance — Current best-known route cost.

blocks.title: Settle X; calculate both tentative distances
blocks.text: Start at X=0. Which neighbour gets distance 4? Which gets 10? Which unsettled vertex should Dijkstra select next?

blocks.title: Settle Y and relax Y→Z
blocks.text: After X: Y=4 (predecessor X), Z=10 (predecessor X). Settle Y=4; candidate cost to Z is 4+3=7 , so improve Z to 7 with predecessor Y.

blocks.title: Finish with the path, not just the cost
blocks.text: Settle Z=7. Predecessors: Z←Y←X . Reverse to X→Y→Z , total cost 7. The direct X→Z cost 10 is longer.
